# Docs: READMEs, TESTING.md and the automation-api wiki page

## What to build

Document the automation API feature (`docs/prd/automation-api.md`) **as it is actually implemented**. This task runs after the engine's plan stage (`--content`, readiness, the approval gate, resume with `--approve-plan` / `--replan`), graph-manager's API tokens and `/api/v1`, and the extension slot (`GM_EXTENSIONS`) are in the codebase. Read the real code first and document what exists: real flag names, real exit-code numbers, real error texts, real route paths and scopes. Where the code differs from the spec, the code wins; note the difference in the wiki page's "Known follow-ups". Do not change any `.ts`/`.tsx` source file in this task, only Markdown.

Files to write: the engine README `packages/graph-execution/README.md` (the full user docs; the root `README.md` is a short monorepo overview that links to it), the root `README.md`, `apps/graph-manager/README.md`, `TESTING.md`, a new `docs/wiki/features/automation-api.md`, and `docs/wiki/index.md`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

Read the implemented code (find it with the greps below; paths are where the spec puts it):

- `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts` — the `.option(...)` calls (around lines 218–252 before this feature) for `--content`, `--refs`, `--no-plan-gate`, `--approve-plan`, `--replan`, `--plan-attempts`, and their usage errors (`--content` with a tasks dir or `--spec`; `--approve-plan`/`--replan` without `--resume`; resume of an `awaiting-approval` run without either flag). `grep -n "content\|refs\|plan-gate\|approve-plan\|replan\|plan-attempts" packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts`
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/errors.ts` — `EXIT_NEEDS_INFO` and `EXIT_AWAITING_APPROVAL` (their numbers). Existing codes: 0 success, 1 review failed, 2 abort, 3 hand-off blocked.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/state/state.ts` — `runStatusSchema` (now with `planning`, `needs-info`, `awaiting-approval`) and the `plan` object of `stateSchema`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/plan/` (all files) — the planner prompt, the plan loop, `result.json` shape, where the spec and tasks are written (`docs/prd/<name>.md`, `.agents/tasks/<name>/`), the `Plan: <name>` commit, `planAttempts`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/config/` (`grep -rn "planAttempts" packages/graph-execution/src`) — the `planAttempts` config key and its default.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts` — the planner mode: `NOT-READY: <ref>` lines and a bare `NOT-READY` line. `grep -n "NOT-READY\|planner" packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts`
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts` — bearer tokens on `/api/v1/*`, the 401 `{"error":"invalid token"}` and 403 `{"error":"missing scope <scope>"}` answers.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts` — `apiTokens` and `apiRuns`.
- `grep -rn "/api/v1\|/api/tokens" apps/graph-manager/src/server` — the token admin routes and every `/api/v1` route: method, path, scope, body, status codes, error texts (e.g. `no provider: pass provider or start a run in this workspace once`), the run object's fields, `idempotencyKey`, `openPr`, the auto-PR loop interval.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` and `apps/graph-manager/src/server/extensions.ts` — `GM_EXTENSIONS`, `GM_EXTENSION_SECRET`, their error messages, the `/ext/<name>/*` proxy, the headers it adds (`X-GM-Extension-Secret`, `X-GM-User`, and any others such as `X-Forwarded-Prefix`), `GET /api/extensions`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/` — `grep -rln "Approvals\|API tokens\|/x/" apps/graph-manager/src/web` for the Approvals page, Settings → API tokens and the extension page, so the UI is described with its real labels.
- `docs/prd/automation-api.md` — the spec: Goals, the Decisions table, Non-goals, Requirements.
- `packages/graph-execution/README.md` — lines 81–126 (Usage: the synopsis block and the options table), 155–165 (the launcher's exit-code table), 215–247 (graph-manager section), 279–314 (config keys table), 543–550 (the "Exit codes" table), 552–569 (Resume), 37–42 (Contents links).
- `README.md` (root, 63 lines) — the monorepo overview with a "graph-manager" section.
- `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — lines 71–96 ("Configuration" env-var table, columns: Env var, Flag, Default (outside Docker), In the image, Meaning), 257–298 ("The app"), 364–378 ("Security", "Limitations").
- `TESTING.md` — lines 20–36 ("Fake provider scripts") and 126–147 (starting graph-manager for tests).
- `docs/wiki/index.md` and `docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md` — the wiki page format to copy exactly: `# Title (ids)`, `## Summary` (with Spec / Tasks / User docs bullets and "These ids are not Jira tickets…"), `## Decisions` table with columns `Decision | Why | Id`, `## Known follow-ups`, `## Code references`, `## Related`, `## Last updated`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/readme/readme.test.ts` and `packages/graph-execution/scripts/render-readme.mjs` — the README is rendered to `dist/README.html` by the build with GitHub-style heading anchors; in-README links like `[x](#automation-api)` must match a heading's slug (lower-case, punctuation removed, spaces → `-`).

## Patterns to follow

**Options table row** (`packages/graph-execution/README.md`, Usage table):

```
| `--reviewers <file>` | Reviewers file (JSON). Default: ... Copied into the run dir at start; not allowed with `--resume`. See [Reviewers file](#reviewers-file-optional). |
```

**Exit codes table** (README "Exit codes"): columns `Code | Meaning | What is kept`.

**graph-manager env table** (`apps/graph-manager/README.md` "Configuration"):

```
| `GM_GITHUB_API_URL` | | `https://api.github.com` | same | The GitHub API base URL (for GitHub Enterprise) |
```

**Wiki decision row** (`docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md`):

```
| There is one hand-written stdio MCP server, `graph-manager-mcp`, ... | It needs no dependency and starts fast. ... | AT-02 |
```

**Style**: short plain sentences, present tense, no marketing words, code in backticks, real outputs in `text` blocks. The repo's docs are written in simple technical English.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Usage synopsis block: add a line `graph-execution --content <file> --provider <name> [--refs <file>] [--no-plan-gate] [--plan-attempts <n>] [run options] [--web]` and extend the resume line with `[--approve-plan | --replan <file>]` (use the real flag spellings from `cli.ts`).
  - Options table: one row each for `--content <file>` (any markdown; an agent writes the spec and tasks first; not allowed with `<tasks-dir>` or `--spec`, exit 2), `--refs <file>` (JSON array `[{ref, url?, title?}]`; only unclear refs are dropped), `--no-plan-gate` (go on without waiting for approval), `--plan-attempts <n>` (planner fix rounds; overrides the config key), `--approve-plan` (with `--resume`, on an `awaiting-approval` run), `--replan <file>` (with `--resume`, feedback markdown; plans again).
  - A new subsection under Usage, `### Starting from plain content` (or similar): the plan stage step by step (readiness check, spec in `docs/prd/<name>.md`, tasks in `.agents/tasks/<name>/`, validation with up to `planAttempts` fix rounds, the `Plan: <name>` commit on the integration branch), the run statuses `planning` → `needs-info` | `awaiting-approval` → `running` → `applied`, what `needs-info` means (questions per ref in `state.json`'s `plan.questions`, `plan.dropped`), and a short example:

    ```bash
    graph-execution --content notes.md --provider claude --web
    graph-execution --resume --run <id> --approve-plan
    graph-execution --resume --run <id> --replan feedback.md
    ```
  - Config table: a `planAttempts` row with its real default.
  - "Exit codes" table: rows for `EXIT_NEEDS_INFO` and `EXIT_AWAITING_APPROVAL` with their real numbers, meanings and what is kept (the run folder and branch; resume an `awaiting-approval` run with `--approve-plan` or `--replan`; `needs-info` is final: start a new run with changed content).
  - "Resume" section: a bullet for `awaiting-approval` runs (needs `--approve-plan` or `--replan <file>`, else the real usage error text) and for runs still in `planning` (plan again from scratch).
  - graph-manager section: one sentence that graph-manager has an automation API (`/api/v1`) with API tokens, linking to graph-manager's README.
  - Add the new section(s) to "Contents" (lines 37–42) with working anchors.
- **GOTCHA**: keep every existing anchor working; check new `#...` links against the heading text.

### UPDATE `README.md` (root)

- **IMPLEMENT**: add a `## Automation API` section after "graph-manager": what it is (start a run from markdown content with a bearer token, poll it, approve it), token setup (Settings → **API tokens** → **Create token**, pick scopes, copy the `gmt_…` token once; or `POST /api/tokens` with the cookie), and a curl example using the real paths and fields:

  ```bash
  TOKEN=gmt_...
  curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"content":"# Add a dark mode toggle\n...","refs":[{"ref":"KAN-41","url":"https://…/browse/KAN-41"}],"provider":"claude","openPr":true}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/v1/workspaces/github~octo~hello/runs        # 201 {"runId":"…","viewUrl":"/runs/…"}
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/v1/runs/<runId>   # {"status":"planning", …}
  ```

  End with a link to the full reference in `apps/graph-manager/README.md`. Verify the workspace id format (`<forge>~<owner>~<repo>`) and the response fields in the code.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - "Configuration" table: rows for `GM_EXTENSIONS` (`name=url,…`, names `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, http(s) URLs, an optional base path; each becomes a nav item and a proxy at `/ext/<name>/`) and `GM_EXTENSION_SECRET` (required when `GM_EXTENSIONS` is set; sent as `X-GM-Extension-Secret`; never passed to terminals or runs). Mention the startup errors.
  - A new `## Automation API` section: API tokens (Settings → API tokens; `gmt_` prefix; only a SHA-256 hash is stored; shown once; last used; revoke; the scopes table `runs:start`, `runs:read`, `runs:approve`, `runs:control`, `runs:pr`, `workspaces:read`), the `/api/tokens` admin routes (cookie only), the `/api/v1` endpoint table (method and path, scope, behaviour, status codes) and the run object, `gate`, `sandbox` default, `provider` default, `openPr` and the auto-PR loop, `idempotencyKey`, the 401/403 error bodies, and that bearer tokens work only on `/api/v1/*`.
  - A new `## Extensions` section: how to add one, what the service receives (the headers, the path without the `/ext/<name>` prefix), that the service must check `X-GM-Extension-Secret` and should only be reachable from graph-manager, that it is shown in an iframe at `/x/<name>` (so it must allow being framed by graph-manager's origin and use relative URLs), and WebSocket support.
  - "The app": the **Approvals** page (count badge, Approve, Request changes with required feedback), refs shown as links on runs, the new status chips, and the extension nav items.
  - "Security": bearer tokens and the extension secret.
- **GOTCHA**: copy the exact UI labels from the components, not from the spec.

### UPDATE `TESTING.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in "Fake provider scripts" (after line 34) a short subsection on the fake planner: `--content` with `--provider fake` writes a fixed one-task spec and tasks; a line `NOT-READY: <ref>` in the content puts that ref in `notReady` with one question; a bare `NOT-READY` line makes the whole content not ready. Give runnable commands in the style of the file (temp repo from `REPO=$(mktemp -d) …`, `$CLI`), e.g. `printf '# Add a file\n' > $REPO/c.md && (cd $REPO && node $CLI --content c.md --provider fake --no-plan-gate)` and the expected `state.json` status and exit code for each case (gate off → `applied`; gate on → `awaiting-approval` and the real exit code; `NOT-READY` → `needs-info`). In the "graph-manager" section, add how to create a token and call `/api/v1` with curl, and how to try an extension (`GM_EXTENSIONS=demo=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` plus `GM_EXTENSION_SECRET`, a one-line `node -e` upstream). Run each command once yourself and write the real outputs.

### CREATE `docs/wiki/features/automation-api.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: copy the structure of `docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md`. Title: `# Automation API: runs from plain content, API tokens, /api/v1 and extensions (AA-01 … AA-NN)`. Summary with bullets: Spec `docs/prd/automation-api.md` (moved to `docs/prd/done/` when the PR is opened), Tasks `.agents/tasks/automation-api/`, User docs (the README sections you wrote), and the sentence "These ids are not Jira tickets: the work was agreed with the user in conversation." A `## Decisions` table (`Decision | Why | Id`) with one row per decision in the spec's Decisions table, ids `AA-01`, `AA-02`, … in order, each worded to match the implemented behaviour (free markdown + refs; one unit without refs; planning as the first stage of the same run; new statuses; exit at `awaiting-approval` and resume with `--approve-plan`/`--replan`; `needs-info` final; gate on by default; planner role with the bundled skills; validation with `planAttempts`; layout and commit; hashes written after planning; token format and hashing; bearer only on `/api/v1`; scopes; one tenant; `sandbox` default; `provider` default; `openPr`; `idempotencyKey`; polling, no webhooks; iframe extension instead of Module Federation; extension secret). `## Known follow-ups`: webhooks or push events, multiple users / per-user tokens / SSO, Module Federation or extension widgets inside graph-manager pages, licensing or premium checks, custom PR branch names, plus every place where the code differs from the spec and anything left open in the run's review notes. `## Code references`: real paths with the main function names (engine CLI, state, errors, `src/plan/*`, fake provider; graph-manager `auth.ts`, `store.ts`, the `/api/v1` and token route files, `config.ts`, `extensions.ts`, the web pages). `## Related`: links to `graph-manager.md`, `sandboxes.md`, `run-options.md`, `../index.md`. `## Last updated`: today's date (`date +%F`).

### UPDATE `docs/wiki/index.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: append `- [Automation API: runs from plain content, API tokens, /api/v1 and extensions (AA-01 … AA-NN)](features/automation-api.md)` at the end of the Features list, with the real last id.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/graph-execution/README.md` documents `--content`, `--refs`, `--no-plan-gate`, `--approve-plan`, `--replan` and `--plan-attempts`, the statuses `planning`, `needs-info`, `awaiting-approval`, and both new exit codes with their real numbers.
- [ ] The root `README.md` has an "Automation API" section with token setup and a curl example of `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/runs` then `GET /api/v1/runs/:id`.
- [ ] `apps/graph-manager/README.md` documents `GM_EXTENSIONS`, `GM_EXTENSION_SECRET`, API tokens with their scopes, and the `/api/v1` endpoints.
- [ ] `TESTING.md` documents the fake provider's planner mode (`NOT-READY: <ref>` and bare `NOT-READY`) with commands that work.
- [ ] `docs/wiki/features/automation-api.md` exists with a decision table (Decision, Why, Id `AA-01`…), known follow-ups (webhooks, multi-user, Module Federation, licensing, custom PR branches) and code references that point at files that exist; it is linked from `docs/wiki/index.md`.
- [ ] Every flag, status, exit code, route, scope, header and error text in the docs matches the code (checked with grep).
- [ ] Every in-page anchor link added resolves to a heading.
- [ ] The README tests and the full suite still pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
# Check that every documented name exists in the code
for f in content refs no-plan-gate approve-plan replan plan-attempts; do grep -q -- "--$f" packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts || echo "missing in cli.ts: --$f"; done
grep -n "EXIT_NEEDS_INFO\|EXIT_AWAITING_APPROVAL" packages/graph-execution/src/state/errors.ts
grep -rn "GM_EXTENSIONS\|GM_EXTENSION_SECRET" apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts
# Every code reference in the wiki page exists
grep -o '`[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]*\.\(ts\|tsx\|mjs\|md\)`' docs/wiki/features/automation-api.md | tr -d '`' | sort -u | while read p; do [ -e "$p" ] || [ -e "apps/graph-manager/src/$p" ] || [ -e "packages/graph-execution/$p" ] || echo "check path: $p"; done

# README build and tests
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm test -w graph-execution -- src/readme/readme.test.ts
node packages/graph-execution/dist/cli.js readme --print | grep -c -- "--content"   # > 0

# Type / lint / all tests
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
```

Known environment failure: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`; ignore only that one.
